about: Old Home Distillers is a family farm distillery on historic Campbell Road in Lebanon, in the rolling hills of Madison County about forty miles southeast of Syracuse. Longtime Lebanon residents Jerry and Marlene Carvell founded it in 2015, turning a hundred-year-old stable into a working stillhouse and later adding a barrel warehouse and grain handling facility. Their sons Aaron and Adam help run it, and three generations of the family now work the property.

As a New York State farm distillery, Old Home works only with New York-grown grain, malt, fruit and sweeteners and does not buy in bulk spirit, so everything in the bottle was fermented and distilled on the farm in traditional copper pot stills. Noche begins as the distillery’s own straight bourbon, which is then finished in tequila barrels. It was released to mark Old Home’s tenth anniversary, in a limited run of just 272 bottles.

The distillery describes notes of mesquite, cardamom and vanilla bean, with almond, leather and piloncillo, the dark unrefined Mexican cane sugar, as the tequila cask works on the bourbon. Old Home suggests it neat, on the rocks or in an Old Fashioned. With only 272 bottles made, it is one of the scarcest whiskeys the family has released.
facts: Straight bourbon from 100% New York-grown grain
